name: Cephalocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Cephalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a cranial sac-like protrusion through a skull defect containing meninges and/or brain tissue
Neuroimaging (MRI or CT) confirming herniation of intracranial contents through a skull defect
Neurological deficits consistent with location and extent of herniation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a cranial sac-like protrusion through a skull defect confirmed by neuroimaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered for syndromic cases.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in occipital or frontal regions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Herniation of meninges and brain tissue through skull defect
searchTerms: brain and membranes bulging through skull
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to brainstem involvement
searchTerms: respiratory problems due to brain damage

imaging: MRI showing herniation of meninges and brain tissue through skull defect
CT scan demonstrating bony defect in skull
Ultrasound prenatal detection of cranial sac protrusion
genetic: Possible association with neural tube defect-related gene mutations
other: Physical examination revealing cranial sac-like mass
Neurological assessment showing deficits correlating with lesion

distinguishingFeatures: Premature fusion of cranial sutures without herniation
Intracranial cystic lesion without skull defect
Herniation of meninges only without brain tissue
Typically smaller sac compared to encephalocele

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of cranial sac
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Cephalocele
UpToDate: Encephalocele: Clinical features and diagnosis
